newsitem.title: USA: CNS working on electro-static allergy gel.
newsitem.headline: CNS working on electro-static allergy gel.

text.p: A clear, odorless gel is under development that can be wiped on the upper lip to set up an electro-static field that prevents inhalation through the nose of mold spores, pollen and dust.
CNS Inc, the company that brought the world the Breathe Right nasal strip, is working on the gel, which dries invisibly after application.
Tentatively named Allergel, it is only in clinical trials, but looks promising, said CNS president Richard Jahnke.

"The product is effective for about half of the people today. We think we can get it to where it will be effective for 70-75 percent of the people by making some improvements," Jahnke told Reuters this week in an interview.

The Breathe Right is an adhesive strip that goes across the bridge of the nose and pulls open the nasal passages. Its meteoric sales growth in the past three years has led to enormous gains for Minneapolis-based CNS.
